chunks.arabic_text: عَمْرُو بْنُ ثَابِتِ بْنِ هُرْمُزَ، أَبُو الْمِقْدَامِ، الْحَدَّادُ، مَوْلَى بَنِي عَجْلَ، كُوفِيٌّ. رَوَى عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ، وَأَبِي جَعْفَرٍ، وَأَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: ʿAmr b. Thābit b. Hurmuz, Abū al-Miqdām, al-Ḥaddād, client of the Banū ʿIjl, Kufan. He narrated from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, Abū Jaʿfar, and Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon them).

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri's *Kitab al-Duafa* highlights ʿAmr ibn Thabit, a Kufan ironsmith whose 'very weak' (*da'if jiddan*) status serves as a critical case study in Shia hadith criticism for distinguishing between mere minor flaws and severe unreliability. His transmission from the third and fourth Imams underscores the rigorous scrutiny applied even to those close to the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the integrity of the chain of narration (*isnad*) in early Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: Who is ʿAmr ibn Thabit ibn Hurmuz and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الْحَدَّادُ: the ironsmith (a kunya or occupational descriptor)
key_terms.ضَعِيفٌ جِدًّا: very weak (a technical term in ʿilm al-rijal)
